To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrostatic stabilization of chloride binding sites in ClC chloride channels is dominated by local interactions, and that the contribution of the protein macrodipoles is negligible.
the ion binding sites are stabilized by hydrogen bonding and by long-range interactions with the protein, and that the contribution of helical macrodipoles is marginal.

the ion occupancy is determined by local interactions, that the electrostatics of chloride binding is dominated by the side-chains of Lys131 and Arg340, and that the macrodipoles of the protein do not contribute to the stabilization of the ions in the binding sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrostatics of chloride binding in a ClC channel homologue.
the electrostatics of chloride ion stabilization in a bacterial ClC-type chloride-selective channel.
the electrostatic stabilization of chloride ions in a chloride channel homologue, and it provides a quantitative analysis of the structural determinants of the binding free energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electrostatic stabilization of chloride ions in EcClC arises from local interactions and from long-range interactions mediated by the protein backbone and by the side-chains of strictly conserved residues.
the stabilization of the ions within the channel is a complex phenomenon that arises from a subtle interplay of local electrostatic interactions and non-local effects.

, in spite the presence of multiple binding sites, chloride binding in the ClC family is dominated by the electrostatic stabilization of single chloride ions, which are located within a narrow and well-defined permeation pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chloride stabilization in EcClC, as in other ClC-type proteins, is mainly achieved through a combination of hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions, with a significant contribution from the side-chain of a single conserved residue, Lys131.

the binding sites of EcClC are stabilized by a delicate balance of electrostatic interactions, which are not limited to local interactions, and which include both favorable and unfavorable interactions.
, in the absence of a detailed atomic-level description of the protein, the electrostatic binding energy of chloride ions in ClC channels can be understood in terms of a few key residues and motifs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite, or rather because of, the high degree of ion repulsion, the binding sites in ClC-type chloride channels are not only electrostatically stabilized but, at the same time, also electrostatically coupled to each other.
the electrostatic interactions in the chloride binding sites of EcClC are dominated by short-range effects.

, while the binding of chloride ions to ClC-type chloride channels is mediated by local interactions, the electrostatic stabilization of the ions is achieved by the concerted action of the whole protein.
